To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear shadowing pattern in neutrino–(A,Z) DIS is significantly different from the one in e–(A,Z), that the shadowing effect is larger at low Q2 than at high Q2 and that the shadowing pattern is different for F3A(x,Q2) than it is for F2A(x,Q2).
the shadowing in the neutrino–nuclear cross sections is a significant effect that should be taken into account in the analysis of neutrino data.

(i) the nuclear modification of the structure function F2A(x,Q2) is significantly larger than that of F3A(x,Q2), (ii) at low and moderate Q2 values, the shadowing effect is significantly larger in F3A(x) than F2A(x).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the shadowing pattern in neutrino–target deeply inelastic scattering in the framework of the factorized pQDC approach.
the study of neutrino–nuclear scattering at low and medium values of Q2, where the shadowing corrections to the nuclear structure functions are expected to be large.
the study of the nuclear modification of the parton distributions in nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NuTeV anomaly cannot be explained by nuclear effects in the structure functions.
nuclear effects in neutrino–target DIS are significant and measurable, and they are expected to be different for different structure functions and for different kinematical regimes.

neutrino–nuclear DIS is a unique tool to study nuclear shadowing and the Q2-dependence of the nuclear enhancement of dynamical power corrections, as well as a powerful test for the validity of pQCD in the small-xB regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear shadowing effects in neutrino–proton and neutrino–nuclear deeply inelastic scattering can be reliably calculated within the framework of the pQCD approach.
the neutrino–nuclear structure function F3A is a very useful probe of the small-xB nuclear shadowing.
the nuclear shadowing effects in the neutrino–nuclear structure functions F2 and F3 are significant at moderate and low values of Q2 and can be as large as a factor of 2–3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrino–nuclear structure functions are modified by a shadowing pattern which is qualitatively similar to that in charged-lepton–nuclear scattering, but which is quantitatively different.
neutrino scattering experiments provide an important tool for studying the nuclear modification of structure functions and for probing the QCD factorization scheme.
nuclear shadowing is a process-dependent effect that cannot be simply parameterized by a universal function.
